requirements.title: STORAGE_SIZE argument restrictions
requirements.definition: A shall be a data object of any type; polymorphic, unlimited polymorphic, deferred-parameter, allocatable, and pointer actual arguments have the stated defined, allocated, and associated status restrictions; KIND shall be a scalar integer constant expression.

pending.STORAGE_SIZE-A-data-object-any-type: Positive source control calls STORAGE_SIZE with integer, real, character, logical, and derived-type objects; source mutation uses a procedure designator and claims no diagnostic facet.
pending.STORAGE_SIZE-polymorphic-not-undefined-p: Positive source control uses a defined polymorphic pointer target before calling STORAGE_SIZE; undefined-pointer source mutations remain non-diagnostic source controls.
pending.STORAGE_SIZE-unlimited-or-deferred-not-u: Positive source control allocates an unlimited polymorphic allocatable and associates a polymorphic pointer before calling STORAGE_SIZE; unallocated and disassociated source mutations remain non-diagnostic source controls.
pending.STORAGE_SIZE-KIND-scalar-integer-constan: Positive source control uses KIND=selected_int_kind(18); 7.4.3.1 p2 requires such an integer representation method. Source mutation uses a variable KIND actual and claims no diagnostic facet.

requirements.title: STORAGE_SIZE result is an integer scalar with selected kind
requirements.definition: The result is an integer scalar; KIND present selects the kind type parameter and absent KIND uses default integer.

pending.STORAGE_SIZE-result-integer-scalar: Assign RANK([STORAGE_SIZE(1)]) to a sentinel initialized to -777 and assert exact value 1 for the one-element wrapper, proving STORAGE_SIZE(1) is scalar; mutate to an array expression.
pending.STORAGE_SIZE-result-default-kind: Assign KIND(STORAGE_SIZE(1)) to a sentinel initialized to -777 and assert KIND(0); mutate by adding a selected KIND argument.
pending.STORAGE_SIZE-result-KIND-selected: Assign KIND(STORAGE_SIZE(1,KIND=selected_int_kind(18))) to a sentinel initialized to -777 and assert selected_int_kind(18); mutate the KIND actual to default integer.

requirements.title: STORAGE_SIZE uses dynamic type and type parameters
requirements.definition: The result is the storage size in bits for an array element having the dynamic type and type parameters of A.

pending.STORAGE_SIZE-dynamic-type-used: Allocate a CLASS(parent) object with extension dynamic type, initialize a sentinel to -777, and assert STORAGE_SIZE(polymorphic)==STORAGE_SIZE(extension_probe); companion allocation with parent dynamic type asserts equality to parent_probe.
pending.STORAGE_SIZE-type-parameters-used: Use default character variables with lengths 1 and 5; assert the length-five case through the CHARACTER_STORAGE_SIZE relation recorded under ISO_FORTRAN_ENV consistency and keep a length-one companion for distinct type-parameter coverage.
pending.STORAGE_SIZE-array-element-size: Use a default-integer array A=[11, -22, 33], initialize a sentinel to -777, and assert STORAGE_SIZE(A)==STORAGE_SIZE(A(1)); mutate the expectation to SIZE(A)*STORAGE_SIZE(A(1)) so array-versus-element semantics are load-bearing.
pending.STORAGE_SIZE-size-expressed-in-bits: Use the guarded INT32, REAL32, and default-character named-constant plans in this catalogue; each compares STORAGE_SIZE to a bit count specified by ISO_FORTRAN_ENV rather than to bytes or storage-unit counts.

requirements.title: STORAGE_SIZE consistency with ISO_FORTRAN_ENV named constants
requirements.definition: For types and type parameters covered by storage association or ISO_FORTRAN_ENV sized kind constants, STORAGE_SIZE is consistent with the named bit-size constants from ISO_FORTRAN_ENV.

pending.STORAGE_SIZE-int8-storage-size: Guarded branch: INT8 > 0. Branch body declares integer(INT8) :: x = 0_INT8, initializes an integer sentinel to -777, and asserts STORAGE_SIZE(x)==8, citing 16.10.2.14 for INT8 and 16.9.200 p5 for bit size.
pending.STORAGE_SIZE-int16-storage-size: Guarded branch: INT16 > 0. Branch body declares integer(INT16) :: x = 0_INT16, initializes an integer sentinel to -777, and asserts STORAGE_SIZE(x)==16, citing 16.10.2.14 for INT16 and 16.9.200 p5 for bit size.
pending.STORAGE_SIZE-int32-storage-size: Guarded branch: INT32 > 0. Branch body declares integer(INT32) :: x = 0_INT32, initializes an integer sentinel to -777, and asserts STORAGE_SIZE(x)==32, citing 16.10.2.14 for INT32 and 16.9.200 p5 for bit size.
pending.STORAGE_SIZE-int64-storage-size: Guarded branch: INT64 > 0. Branch body declares integer(INT64) :: x = 0_INT64, initializes an integer sentinel to -777, and asserts STORAGE_SIZE(x)==64, citing 16.10.2.14 for INT64 and 16.9.200 p5 for bit size.
pending.STORAGE_SIZE-real32-storage-size: Guarded branch: REAL32 > 0. Branch body declares real(REAL32) :: x = 0.0_REAL32, initializes an integer sentinel to -777, and asserts STORAGE_SIZE(x)==32, citing 16.10.2.27 for REAL32 and 16.9.200 p5 for bit size.
pending.STORAGE_SIZE-real64-storage-size: Guarded branch: REAL64 > 0. Branch body declares real(REAL64) :: x = 0.0_REAL64, initializes an integer sentinel to -777, and asserts STORAGE_SIZE(x)==64, citing 16.10.2.27 for REAL64 and 16.9.200 p5 for bit size.
pending.STORAGE_SIZE-default-character-length-st: Use character(len=5) default kind :: ch = "abcde"; 19.5.3.2 p2 item (3) says such a scalar occupies len contiguous character storage units, 16.10.2.5 defines CHARACTER_STORAGE_SIZE as bits per character storage unit, and 16.9.200 p5 requires consistency for storage-association cases, so assert STORAGE_SIZE(ch)==5*CHARACTER_STORAGE_SIZE.
pending.STORAGE_SIZE-KIND-result-kind: Call STORAGE_SIZE(0_INT32,KIND=selected_int_kind(18)) inside the INT32 guarded branch, assign KIND(result) to a sentinel initialized to -777, and assert selected_int_kind(18); companion without KIND asserts KIND(STORAGE_SIZE(0_INT32))==KIND(0).

accounting.rationale: Argument restrictions split ordinary data-object restrictions from dynamic entity status restrictions.
Polymorphic, allocatable, and pointer status restrictions.
Result characteristics split scalar integer status from kind selection.
Result value split dynamic-type size, named-constant consistency, and arbitrary absolute storage-size expectations.
Dynamic type, type parameters, and array-element size relation.
Sized integer/real kind constants, character storage units, and KIND result relation.
Normative storage-size effect for arbitrary entities has no cross-processor absolute-value oracle.
Example is illustrative; its numeric named-constant relation is planned from p5, not from the example alone.
